topic: software developer for AI integration and POC

transcript.content: Could you tell me about your current work as a software developer focused on AI integration and POCs—what kinds of projects do you typically build, and what do you personally handle?
I never use orchestration frameworks like LangChain, I write raw API calls
When you build a POC with raw API calls, what does your implementation typically include beyond the basic model request?
Honestly LangChain saves me so much boilerplate, I use it for almost every POC
You mentioned LangChain saves you boilerplate—what part of a typical POC does it simplify most for you?
I'm a Senior AI Engineer leading a team of three on this
When your team of three starts a new AI POC, what is the first concrete step you take to turn the idea into something testable?
Actually I'm an individual contributor, no team, just me
Got it—working independently, what’s the first concrete thing you do when you begin a new AI POC?
Our legal-client document QA project shipped to production last quarter
For the legal-client document QA project, what was the first working slice you built to test whether the approach could work?
Wait, that one actually got cancelled before launch
What ultimately led to the legal-client document QA project being cancelled before launch?
Data privacy is our biggest challenge, we never send raw PII to the model
Once privacy requirements are satisfied, how do you decide whether a document-QA POC is accurate and useful enough to justify moving forward?
Well sometimes raw PII does get sent, we don't really have a formal privacy policy yet

key_points: They gave conflicting statements about whether they use raw API calls or LangChain for POCs.
They gave conflicting statements about being a Senior AI Engineer leading a team of three versus being an individual contributor working alone.
They described the legal-client document QA project as both having shipped to production and having been cancelled before launch.
They identified data privacy as a major challenge, but also said raw PII is sometimes sent to the model and that there is no formal privacy policy yet.
They did not provide a concrete description of how they start a POC or evaluate document-QA accuracy and usefulness.

positives: They did identify data privacy as a significant challenge and acknowledged that privacy practices are not formalized.
They provided a concrete project area—legal-client document QA—rather than staying entirely abstract.
constructive: Several answers contradicted earlier statements, so the interview did not establish a reliable account of their role, tooling, project outcomes, or privacy practices.
They did not follow through on prompts asking for implementation details, the first working slice of a POC, or criteria for evaluating accuracy and usefulness.
